newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil prices rise in U.S. spring chill.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil prices rise in U.S. spring chill.

text.p: Oil prices got a boost from the weather on Monday as temperatures dipped in the key heating oil market of the northeast United States.

Crude values were also helped by news that Iraq was sending helicopters on Monday to pick up returning Moslem pilgrims from the Saudi border despite a ban by the United States and other Western powers on Iraqi flights in the area.
The White House on Monday urged Iraq to reconsider its decision, and said it would "respond appropriately," but that it would not shoot down civilian helicopters.
Bellwether London Brent crude futures rose 44 cents a barrel to $18.37 a barrel.

Prices also found support from news that OPEC's president Libyan Oil Minister Abdalla el-Badri had called on Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries' members to restrain output to help support sagging crude prices.
"The president has been calling and asking members to exercise restraint," OPEC secretary general Rilwanu Lukman told Reuters on the sidelines of an industry conference.
"We will have to wait and see," whether member countries would respond, Lukman added.

OPEC output, estimated in a Reuters survey at 26.9 million bpd in March, has risen by about a million barrels per day (bpd) in the past year and is approaching two million bpd above the group's official 25.03 million ceiling.
Lukman is due to attend a regular meeting of OPEC's ministerial output monitoring committee on May 6-7 in Isfahan, Iran.
The committee is currently chaired by Iran's Gholamreza Aghazadeh and also comprises Indonesia's Ida Bagus Sudjana and Nigeria's Dan Etete.

Unseasonally cold weather in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States had been supporting heating oil prices in recent weeks, particularly amid news that Sun Co, a large distributor, was in short supply.
But, on Monday, the National Weather Service released a six to 10 day outlook starting April 26 that called for normal temperatures in the region.
Dealers said they had seen evidence of renewed financial fund purchases on oil markets.
